stories.body: Oman says its mediation with Iran on securing navigation through the Strait of Hormuz is progressing constructively, with discussions focused on a transit route jointly administered by the two coastal states. Iran's foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, said negotiations were nearing their final stages but stressed that reopening the waterway would depend on further conditions. Tehran is demanding compensation for war damage, an end to US threats and the naval blockade of Iranian ports, sanctions relief and the release of frozen assets; it has also sought transit fees. The strait has been effectively closed since the US-Israel war on Iran began, disrupting a route that normally carries about a fifth of global oil and gas flows.
stories.headline: Iran sets conditions for reopening the Strait of Hormuz as talks continue

stories.body: At least four people, including a three-year-old child, were killed in overnight Russian attacks on Kyiv and surrounding areas, Ukrainian officials said. President Volodymyr Zelensky said attacks and frontline shelling had killed 13 people over 24 hours and warned that Ukraine could enter winter with virtually no functioning thermal power plants. Russia has intensified drone and missile attacks while exploiting depleted Ukrainian air defences; Ukraine has continued long-range strikes on Russian oil facilities, including another refinery.
stories.headline: Russian strikes kill civilians near Kyiv as Ukraine warns of a winter power crisis

stories.body: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey signed the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Mecca, declaring that an armed attack on one member will be considered an attack on all three. The leaders presented the pact as collective deterrence and said it targets no country, but analysts view it as a strategic signal shaped by the US-Israel war on Iran, attacks on Gulf exporters and doubts about US regional protection. The agreement builds on a 2025 Saudi-Pakistan deal and long-standing defence-industrial ties, though analysts say integrated military capabilities and specific obligations remain unclear and could take years to develop.
stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey sign a mutual defence pact

stories.body: A fast-moving, out-of-control wildfire in British Columbia has forced more than 20,000 people from Summerland, Peachland and nearby communities west of Okanagan Lake. The Bald Range fire expanded rapidly after being reported on Friday, burning roughly 9,500 hectares and prompting a provincial state of emergency as hot, windy and drought conditions fuel more than 100 fires. Authorities said some residents had to be rescued after being trapped, while the number of destroyed homes remains unknown. The evacuation includes care-facility residents and animals, as crews struggle with one of the region's quickest-growing fires.
stories.headline: Fast-moving British Columbia wildfire forces more than 20,000 people to flee

stories.body: Spain has begun temporary checks on air and sea travellers arriving from Italy, escalating a dispute triggered by Italy's own restrictions after a mass crossing into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta. The month-long Spanish measures, due to run through September 7 unless circumstances change, are described as random and have initially focused on a small share of passengers from third countries. Madrid says Italy's fear that migrants entering Ceuta could move onward through Schengen is unfounded, while Rome says its controls are intended to prevent that movement. Most of the roughly 70,000 to 78,000 migrants who crossed into Ceuta have returned, but many minors remain.
stories.headline: Spain imposes temporary checks on arrivals from Italy amid Ceuta migration dispute

stories.body: The US Senate confirmed President Donald Trump's former personal lawyer Todd Blanche as attorney general by a 50-49 vote, ending a prolonged fight over the acting attorney general's nomination. Republican Senators Susan Collins and Lisa Murkowski joined Democrats in opposition, while Senator Bill Cassidy cast the deciding vote. Critics cited Blanche's role in releasing Epstein-related records, concerns over the Justice Department's politicisation, and a proposed $1.8 billion fund for people alleging government persecution; Blanche pledged to abandon the proposal after opposition from senators.
stories.headline: US Senate narrowly confirms Todd Blanche as attorney general

stories.body: More than 300,000 Haitians in the United States have lost Temporary Protected Status and face possible detention or deportation unless they qualify for another immigration remedy. A federal judge's order blocking the termination is no longer in effect after a Supreme Court ruling opened the way for the administration to end the programme. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said enforcement was under way, while advocates argue that deporting people to Haiti is unsafe given the country's violence and instability. The change is also spreading fear through Haitian communities and threatens workers in sectors including health care, construction and agriculture.
stories.headline: Haitians face arrest and deportation risks after US ends TPS protections

stories.body: A pilot and a crew member were killed when their Sikorsky S-64 Skycrane helicopter crashed Friday while fighting the Widemouth 2 fire near Richfield, Utah. Extreme fire behaviour and steep terrain initially prevented rescue teams from reaching the wreckage; the bodies were recovered Saturday. The crash started another fire that merged with the existing blaze, which has burned more than 111,000 acres in Fishlake National Forest and was 24% contained. Fire managers briefly paused operations after the crash before resuming the response and maintaining evacuations and road closures.
stories.headline: Two crew members die in helicopter crash while fighting Utah wildfire

stories.body: Lake Mead has reached a historic low water level, underscoring the worsening strain on the Colorado River system and its major reservoirs. The visible mineral bathtub ring around the lake near Hoover Dam illustrates how far water levels have fallen. Low levels at Lake Mead and Lake Powell have led the US Bureau of Reclamation to propose action intended to avert a broader Colorado River crisis, with consequences for the communities, farms and infrastructure dependent on the river.
stories.headline: Lake Mead reaches a historic low as pressure on the Colorado River intensifies

stories.body: Americans increasingly say extreme heat is changing daily routines, travel and outdoor activities, according to an AP-NORC poll. Heat also poses a growing problem for aviation: hot, thin air reduces lift and engine performance, sometimes forcing airlines to reduce passenger, cargo or fuel loads or delay departures. American Airlines sought volunteers to leave a Las Vegas flight when temperatures reached 114F in July. Airports at high elevation or with shorter runways can face similar restrictions at lower temperatures, and researchers say climate change could make the disruptions more frequent.
stories.headline: Extreme heat disrupts daily life and could increasingly delay US flights

stories.body: The mass arrival of migrants in Ceuta has left a humanitarian and political crisis despite the return of most of those who crossed from Morocco. Reports differ sharply on how many people remain, with the central government estimating about 2,500 and Ceuta's president, Juan Jesús Vivas, putting the figure at 8,000 to 11,000, including many minors. Vivas has called the situation unsustainable, demanded additional police, immigration resources and a continued military presence, and urged returns to Morocco. Media investigations also point to warnings, legal confusion over maritime border controls and online misinformation that preceded the crossing, in which dozens of people died.
stories.headline: Ceuta migration crisis deepens tensions between Spain, Morocco and the EU

stories.body: Authorities expect millions of people and as many as 1.5 million additional journeys for Spain's first total solar eclipse since 1912, with the best views in a band across 32 provinces. In Catalonia, officials are preparing traffic, civil-protection and policing measures as visitors head for Tarragona, the Terres de l'Ebre and Lleida, where totality will last roughly one to one-and-a-half minutes. Two key natural parks will close because of high wildfire risk, and southbound truck traffic on part of the AP-7 will be restricted on eclipse day. Officials are also warning viewers to use proper eye protection and urging visitors to travel early.
stories.headline: Spain prepares for August 12 total solar eclipse amid crowd, traffic and safety concerns

stories.body: Spain's Civil Guard is investigating the origins of two July megafires that authorities say were deliberately set: one near Burgohondo in Ávila, which burned more than 50,000 hectares, and another in Vall d'Uixó, Castellón, which burned 9,568 hectares and damaged part of the Sierra de Espadán natural park. In Vall d'Uixó, two fires began at separate sites within about an hour, shortly after firefighters had contained the first. Heat, wind and vegetation dried by four heat waves created conditions that allowed the flames to spread rapidly, while investigators seek to establish who was responsible.
stories.headline: Investigators examine origins of Spain's destructive July megafires

stories.body: Spain's temporary border checks on travellers arriving from Italy began at midnight, initially at major airports and later expanding to other airports and ports. A hundred National Police officers checked 199 third-country nationals arriving on 12 flights by late Saturday, generally inspecting 5% to 10% of passengers on each flight. The checks, in place until September 7 unless revised, are random rather than systematic and are conducted at the aircraft gate; EU citizens are exempt. Madrid says the move responds to Italy's refusal to end its own controls on travellers from Spain after the Ceuta migration crisis.
stories.headline: Spain's checks on Italy arrivals begin at airports with limited inspections

stories.body: Passengers arriving at Barcelona-El Prat from Italy encountered limited, random document checks on the first day of Spain's temporary controls, with most describing the process as quick and some flights apparently unaffected. At the same time, an indefinite CGT strike by Groundforce Barcelona ground staff has caused more than 50 flight cancellations in five days, according to the union, and left an estimated 1,500 to 2,000 bags stranded. The strike affects baggage check-in and delivery, boarding and flight coordination, adding queues and uncertainty for passengers independently of the new border measures.
stories.headline: Barcelona airport sees random Italy-arrival checks as Groundforce strike disrupts flights

stories.body: Barcelona is forecast to face another very hot and humid day, with temperatures nearing 34C in parts of the city and exceeding 35C in the Vallès. Catalonia's weather service has issued an intense-heat warning from 8am to 8pm, with a maximum danger level of three out of six. Weak to moderate sea breezes may offer limited relief, while another torrid night is expected. Forecasters say heat and humidity will remain high through the week, with potential cloud and thunderstorm uncertainty around the August 12 eclipse.
stories.headline: Barcelona faces another intense heat day under an official alert

stories.body: Renfe says a recovery plan has substantially improved the operation of lifts and escalators at its stations after failures made the situation unacceptable in early 2025. Only 51% of lifts were working on average in February through April last year, while nearly half of escalators were out of service at their worst point. The company now reports 85% of lifts and 95% of escalators operating. Catalonia's transport minister, Sílvia Paneque, blamed shortcomings by former contractor Schindler; a new contract with TKE has begun repairs and Renfe has filed a claim over accumulated defects.
stories.headline: Renfe says recovery plan has improved reliability of station lifts and escalators
